details: The US Producer Price Index (PPI) for May rose 1.1% monthly and 6.5% year-over-year, surpassing Wall Street forecasts. This hotter-than-expected wholesale inflation data suggests persistent price pressures, increasing the likelihood that the Federal Reserve will maintain a hawkish monetary policy stance or consider further rate hikes. Bitcoin experienced a brief dip following the news.
title: US PPI Soars to 6.5% in May, Fueling Hawkish Fed Policy Concerns

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) raised its main deposit facility rate by 25 basis points to 2.40%, marking its first interest rate increase since July 2023. The move, largely anticipated by markets, aims to combat rising inflation driven by geopolitical tensions affecting energy costs. Higher interest rates typically reduce liquidity in financial markets, which can be a negative for risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: ECB Hikes Rates by 25 Bps Amid Inflation Concerns

details: The US Consumer Price Index (CPI) for May increased by 0.5% monthly and 4.2% year-over-year, largely aligning with economists' predictions. While still elevated, the CPI meeting expectations provided some relief to markets, contributing to a brief recovery in Bitcoin after earlier losses triggered by the hotter PPI data.
title: US CPI in Line with Expectations, Bitcoin Recovers Briefly

details: Escalating geopolitical tensions, particularly concerning the US and Iran, continue to fuel a "risk-off" environment in financial markets. This, combined with a sustained period of Bitcoin ETF outflows, indicates institutional investors are reducing their exposure to risk assets. The outflows are among the longest streaks recorded, contributing to bearish sentiment and increased volatility in the cryptocurrency market.
title: Geopolitical Risks & ETF Outflows Drive Crypto Sell-off
